title: Why fizzy drinks go flat
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do fizzy drinks go flat?
Why do warm drinks go flat faster?
Why does a shaken bottle spray?

explain.say: A fizzy drink is made by forcing carbon dioxide gas into it under high pressure. In the sealed bottle the gas stays dissolved, hidden in the liquid.
When you open it, the pressure suddenly drops with a hiss. The liquid now holds more gas than it can keep at normal air pressure.
The extra gas comes out as bubbles, which grow on tiny scratches and specks in the glass, rise and pop at the surface.
Bit by bit the dissolved gas escapes until the drink is flat. Warm drinks go flat faster, because warm liquids hold less gas.

faq.q: How is the fizz put into drinks?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide is pumped into the cold drink under pressure, a few times normal air pressure, and the bottle is sealed so it stays dissolved.

faq.q: Why do warm drinks go flat faster?
faq.a: Gases dissolve less well in warm liquids, so a warm drink lets its carbon dioxide go much faster than a cold one.
asks: Why keep fizzy drinks in the fridge?

faq.q: Why do bubbles form on the sides of the glass?
faq.a: Bubbles need a place to start, such as a tiny scratch, a speck of dust or a fibre. Gas collects there and grows into a bubble.
asks: Where do the bubbles in a drink come from?

faq.q: Does screwing the cap back on help?
faq.a: Yes. Gas builds up in the space above the drink, the pressure rises, and less escapes from the liquid. It works less well when the bottle is nearly empty.
asks: How do you keep a drink fizzy?

faq.q: Why does shaking a bottle make it spray?
faq.a: Shaking mixes in lots of tiny bubbles. When you open the bottle, gas rushes into all of them at once, and they swell and push the drink out.

facts: A sealed bottle of fizzy drink holds carbon dioxide at a few times normal air pressure.
Water at 0 degrees Celsius can dissolve about twice as much carbon dioxide as water at 20 degrees.
